Cc: James Park <james.park@regenthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regent Health — DPA & SCCs: transfer impact addendum and roles

Hi team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a redline of Redwood's standard DPA and a short note on how we propose handling the SCCs + transfer impact addendum. The two items we're hoping to close quickly are:

- Role delegation matrix (controller/processor/processor-subprocessor entries) — see table on page 2 of the redline.
- Transfer impact addendum language to cover restricted transfers to third countries and the fallback SCCs versioning.

Actions we're proposing: short path-forward below — please confirm if that works on your end.

1) Regent legal to confirm any carve-outs for hosted private deployment (we flagged the VPC/on-prem exception).
2) Redwood legal (cc'd) to accept or suggest targeted redlines to the SCCs addendum.
3) If both agree, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet with the DPA + Order Form exhibit to sign.

I've attached: Regent_DPA_redline_v4.docx (tracked), Regent_SCCs_addendum.pdf and a stub SOC2 report for reference.

Would appreciate a reply by EOD Tue so we can include this in next-week's onboarding schedule.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Regent Health Legal <legal@regenthealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Park <james.park@regenthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 14:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Regent Health — DPA & SCCs: transfer impact addendum and roles

Markus,

Appreciate the redline and the quick summary. We reviewed the document and have three primary concerns before we can move to signature:

1) Subprocessor notice: we require 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors that will process EEA-originated data. Your current clause is 10 days / "as available".
2) Transfer impact addendum: we need explicit language that references the most recent Commission Implementing Decision for SCCs and an explicit fallback to our additional safeguards (encryption + contractual commitments) if a given jurisdiction is found to be high risk.
3) Audit rights: our security team is asking for a limited audit right (remote assessment annually) or equivalent evidence (updated SOC2 + penetration test summary).

I've attached a tracked version with our suggested edits and inline comments. See attached: Regent_DPA_comments_from_RH.docx and a short memo explaining acceptable evidence.

If you can accept the 30-day subprocessor notice and add the Commission Decision reference, we should be able to finalize rapidly. Otherwise we'll need a short escalation call with legal and security.

Regards,

Regent Health Legal
[Attachment: Regent_DPA_comments_from_RH.docx] [Attachment: RH_Evidence_Memo.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Regent Health Legal <legal@regenthealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regent Health — DPA & SCCs: transfer impact addendum and roles

Thanks for the notes — Karthik from Redwood Legal here. I reviewed your tracked changes (thanks), and a few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Subprocessor notice: we can accept 30 days' notice for EEA-originated data where Regent has a documented regional requirement. For hosted accounts on Redwood Dedicated we will retain the 10-day operational notice for urgent infra subproc deployments; we'll add a carve-out to surface urgent patches but otherwise 30 days will apply.

- Commission Implementing Decision: we'll add an explicit reference to the most recent decision and include language that the parties will work in good faith to agree additional safeguards where required (we will reference encryption-at-rest and TLS in transit + contractual obligations).

- Audit rights: we cannot support on-site audits, but we can offer an annual remote security questionnaire, updated SOC2 report (we'll provide within 10 business days of request) and a summary penetration test report under NDA. If Regent requires stronger terms, we can include a defined escalation path to an independent assessor for extraordinary circumstances.

I've attached a proposed short addendum that folds your comments into our redline (file: RGN_DPA_compromise_v1.docx). Key change log in the top margin. 

Proposed next steps:
- Regent confirms whether the 30-day / 10-day carve-out approach is acceptable.
- If agreed, we will prepare the final DPA + SCCs addendum and route via DocuSign.
- If not, schedule a brief legal + security call (30 minutes).

Markus and Monica — flagging for visibility and for Monica to create the HubSpot deal note and DocuSign packet when we get confirmation.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RGN_DPA_compromise_v1.docx]
